title: Transactional data
planning: Write domain invariants explicitly before implementation: valid quantities, allowed states, ownership, available balance or inventory, and replay behavior.
Treat client-supplied prices, totals, ownership, and status as untrusted; resolve authoritative values on the server at mutation time.
Use decimal or integer minor-unit storage for money rather than binary floating point.
Make validation and mutation atomic with an appropriate database transaction or conditional update; account for concurrent requests and retries.
Define idempotency and audit requirements for mutations that must not execute twice.
checks: Test zero, negative, fractional, non-finite, malformed, and very large inputs as well as invalid enum values.
Run concurrent mutation tests proving balance, holdings, inventory, or capacity cannot go negative or exceed limits.
Test rollback on downstream failure and replay of the same request where duplicate execution would be harmful.
Verify calculations at rounding boundaries with deterministic fixtures.
review: Reject read-check-write sequences outside a transaction, Float money columns, truthiness-based numeric validation, and duplicate calculation implementations.
Confirm historical reports never use future values as fallback data and never present estimated values as authoritative without labeling them.
